related.id: MB-143 Excision of a skin lesion
related.why: When a lump is removed, and when it must not be
The same description applied to the neck

brief.scenario: Mr Owen, 50, has a lump on his upper back that he thinks has grown over the past six months.
brief.task: Examine the lump. You will be stopped at 6 minutes to present your findings and answer questions.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Describe everything before naming anything, then check for red flags.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Calling a soft lump a lipoma and missing that it's large and growing.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Measure it. "May I measure the lump with a tape?"

grid.label: Preparation
grid.fail: Starts palpating without introduction, consent or asking about pain.
grid.pass: Introduces, confirms identity, explains, gains consent, asks about pain, cleans hands, exposes adequately.
grid.high: Positions the patient so the lump and surrounding area are fully visible and relaxed.

grid.label: Inspection
grid.pass: Site, size (measured), shape, colour, overlying skin, punctum, scars.
grid.high: Compares with the other side and inspects the draining lymph node area.

grid.label: Palpation
grid.borderline: Checks consistency but not attachment to deeper structures.
grid.pass: Temperature, tenderness, surface, edge, consistency, fluctuance, attachment to skin and deeper tissues.
grid.high: Tests attachment to muscle with the muscle tensed, and checks the slip sign.

grid.label: Special tests
grid.pass: Transillumination, pulsatility, compressibility, reducibility, and auscultation.
grid.high: Explains what each separates, e.g. expansile pulsation suggests an aneurysm, transmitted pulsation does not.

grid.label: Nodes and neurovascular
grid.high: Checks distal neurovascular status for limb lumps, and says so for this site.

grid.label: Presentation and differential
grid.fail: Names a diagnosis without a description.
grid.pass: Describes the lump, then gives a differential: lipoma, epidermoid cyst, soft tissue sarcoma.
grid.high: Names the red flags present: over 5 cm, increasing in size, deep, painful.

grid.label: Next steps
grid.fail: Plans to excise it in a minor operations list.
grid.pass: Unexplained lump increasing in size: urgent direct access ultrasound.
grid.high: Explains that if sarcoma is suspected, biopsy should be planned by the sarcoma service, not done as a local excision.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Starts pressing on the lump without asking about pain.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It's about the size of a golf ball.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Book it for excision on a minor ops list.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Hello, I'm Dr Patel. Can I confirm your name and date of birth? I'd like to examine the lump on your back; is it painful at all? [Consent; cleans hands; exposes the back.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Inspects.] May I measure it? [Measures 6 by 5 cm.] The skin over it looks normal, with no punctum or scars.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Temperature, tenderness, surface, edge, consistency, fluctuance; checks whether the skin moves over it and whether it moves over the deeper tissues.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Transilluminates; checks for pulsation, compressibility and reducibility; listens with the stethoscope.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Examines the axillary nodes.] Thank you. [Cleans hands.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: A 6 by 5 cm soft, lobulated, non-tender lump over the right scapula, not attached to skin, mobile over deeper tissues, not transilluminating or pulsatile, no nodes. The differential is lipoma, epidermoid cyst or soft tissue sarcoma.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: As it's unexplained and growing, an urgent direct access ultrasound.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Hello, I'm Dr Patel. Can I confirm your name and date of birth? I'd like to look at and feel the lump, and check the glands nearby. Is it sore? Could you sit forward with your arms relaxed? [Cleans hands.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Compares both sides; measures 6 by 5 cm; looks for punctum, scars, skin change; inspects the axillae.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Full palpation.] Could you push your hands together in front of you? [Tenses the underlying muscle; checks mobility; slip sign at the edge.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Transillumination, pulsatility, compressibility, reducibility, auscultation.] There's no pulsation, so an aneurysm is unlikely.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Axillary nodes.] As it's on the trunk, there's no distal neurovascular check to add. Thank you. [Cleans hands.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A 6 by 5 cm soft, lobulated lump over the right scapula, mobile, not attached to skin, and it stays mobile with the muscle tensed. It feels like a lipoma, but it's over 5 cm and growing, which are red flags for sarcoma. I can't call it benign on examination.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: An urgent direct access ultrasound. If that suggests sarcoma, he needs a suspected cancer pathway referral, and any biopsy should be planned by the sarcoma service, not a local excision.

failures.consequence: Misses the tests that separate cyst, vascular lesion and hernia.

failures.move: Listing a large, deep lump for local excision without imaging.
failures.consequence: Risks an unplanned excision of a sarcoma, which compromises later curative surgery.

recovery.line: Let me describe it properly first: size, shape, surface, edge, consistency and attachments.

recovery.when: You're not sure what it is
recovery.line: It feels benign, but it has red flags, so I'd image it before anyone excises it.

knowledge.fact: Red flags for soft tissue sarcoma: increasing size, over 5 cm, deep, painful.
Consider urgent direct access ultrasound for an unexplained lump that is increasing in size.
Lipoma: soft, lobulated, slip sign. Epidermoid cyst: attached to skin, often with a punctum.

recall.think: Describe, test, then look for red flags.
do: Attachment to skin and to deeper tissue
recall.finish: Urgent ultrasound; no local excision if sarcoma is possible.

partner.opening: Please examine this lump. I'll stop you at 6 minutes.
partner.actorBrief: You are Mr Owen, 50. The lump appeared about a year ago and your wife says it's got bigger. It isn't painful. No weight loss.

reveals.finding: Soft, lobulated, non-tender, not attached to skin, mobile, including with muscle tensed.
Does not transilluminate; not pulsatile; not compressible or reducible.
Say: "Please stop there and present your findings."

push.question: What's your differential?
push.expect: Lipoma, epidermoid cyst, soft tissue sarcoma.

push.question: Which features worry you?
push.expect: Over 5 cm and increasing in size.

push.question: What would you do next?
push.expect: Urgent direct access ultrasound; no local excision.

curveballs.prompt: The GP wants to remove it in the practice.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Not until imaging excludes sarcoma; an unplanned excision can compromise treatment.
I'd check whether it's expansile, which suggests an aneurysm, or transmitted.
